HSV.why: Named color model/space in common use; very widely known, so first-pick tier is right.

Ekta Space PS 5.why: Real wide-gamut RGB space (Pointer's Ekta Space PS5) used in raw converters. Obscure, so a deep tier fits.

PAL/SECAM.why: Two distinct TV colour encodings joined by a slash, not one named kind. The alias pal_secam is an identifier, not a name. Keep PAL and SECAM as separate entries if they are wanted.

ICaCb.why: I cannot confirm this as an established colour space name, and the rule says to reject when unsure it exists.

Panasonic V-Gamut.why: Named gamut of Panasonic's V-Log camera pipeline. Specialist knowledge, so Race condition fits.

CAM02-UCS.why: Named uniform colour space derived from CIECAM02 in the colour science literature. Specialist tier fits.

DCDM XYZ.why: DCDM is the SMPTE digital cinema distribution master, encoded in XYZ. Specialist tier fits.

Apple Wide Gamut RGB.why: Named ColorSync working space. The alias 'Apple Wide Gamut' is a shortened form and is acceptable as an alias.

IPT.why: Ebner and Fairchild's IPT colour space, a named perceptual space in the literature. Specialist tier fits.

CAM16-UCS.why: Named uniform colour space from the CAM16 appearance model. Specialist tier fits.

ECI RGB v2.why: Named European Color Initiative RGB working space. Specialist tier fits.

sRGB.why: The default web and display colour space (IEC 61966-2-1). Well known to developers, so a shallow tier fits.

HSL.why: Hue-saturation-lightness colour model, familiar from CSS and design tools. First-pick tier fits.

Russell RGB.why: Named RGB colour space in the standard lists of RGB spaces. Obscure, so a deep tier fits.

Hunter Lab.why: Named Hunter Lab colour space (1948) used in colour measurement. Domain-expert tier fits.

NTSC.why: Named NTSC colour encoding standard, widely known from TV history. 'NTSC color' and 'NTSC 1953' are acceptable aliases.

Canon Cinema Gamut.why: Named Canon cinema camera gamut. Specialist tier fits.

SMPTE-C.why: Named SMPTE C phosphor standard for NTSC-era displays. Domain-expert tier fits.

ACES.why: Named Academy Color Encoding System. The alias ACEScg is a separate working space (AP1) folded in as an alias, which is borderline but tolerable. Domain-expert tier fits.

Linear RGB.why: Named kind (linear-light RGB), but it is a generic description of a state rather than a single space, so membership is borderline. A Null pointer exception tier is too shallow; it is a specialist concept, closer to Memory leak.
